newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bank weighs new jumbo securitisation issue.
newsitem.headline: French bank weighs new jumbo securitisation issue.

text.p: French bank Credit Lyonnais said on Wednesday it was considering launching another jumbo securitisation issue to repackage part of a costly loan it was forced to make when it was bailed out by the state two years ago.
"We've been sounding out the market. We're looking at launching such an operation after the summer but nothing has been decided," said a spokesman for the state-controlled bank.

His statement came after business daily Les Echos reported Credit Lyonnais was planning to securitise another 40 billion francs of the 119 billion franc loan it made in 1995 to state-backed holding company EPFR.
The agency was set up by the state to house the bank's bad assets and give Credit Lyonnais a clean start after a lending spree that almost brought its collapse in the early 1990s.

Last year the bank scored a hit with investors around the world when it securitised 40 billion francs of the loan in what was the largest ever sale of non-government bonds in international capital markets.
Les Echos said the new issue would be in one single tranche unlike last year's operation which was divided into four tranches.
The loan to EPFR carries an implicit state guarantee, ensuring the securitisation issue a top-flight triple A credit rating, because the agency was set up by the state.
The spokesman said the size of the possible issue had not been decided and that no banks had been authorised yet to examine how to carry out such a transaction.
The operation would help the bank better manage its balance sheet.
But it would not eliminate the penalty aspect of the loan which the state required the bank to make at below market interest rates to compensate for its expansion drive.
"It would be a balance sheet management exercise," said the spokesman for the bank which has made a strong recovery from its huge losses.

The terms of the loan turned out to be so harsh that it threatened to drag the bank back into loss and the previous conservative government was forced to neutralise the cost, estimated at three billion francs this year.
The European Commission is now considering whether to approve the move under a restructuring plan for the bank submitted by the new Socialist government.
Securitisation is relatively new to Europe despite being widely used in the United States to repackage debt into negotiable shares.
Credit Lyonnais has been a pioneer of securitisation in France but last year's asset-backed issue represented an ambitious leap forward.
